dedupe_keys.name: language barriers in 9 1 1 medical calls coded call audio and dispatch data for 788 calls icpsr

description: This dataset codes 788 real 9-1-1 medical calls with language barriers received by four emergency communication centres, to study how over-the-phone interpretation affects medical dispatch. It is distributed by the Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR) with a DOI. Call audio and computer-aided dispatch records were coded for communication processes, call characteristics and outcomes; 85 percent of calls are advanced life support and 43 percent used the Language Line service. Outcomes include time to first medical dispatch, time to address completion, time to pre-arrival instructions, time to first arrival on scene, triage errors and caller compliance, with covariates such as emergency location and caller relationship. Coverage is four United States centres. The study found that all time-based dispatch outcomes were significantly delayed when interpretation was used. Access is through the ICPSR archive, which is free but needs a user account and acceptance of its terms of use; the licence is not stated in the DataCite record read. Caveats: the sample is four centres and high-acuity calls, and audio is not shared. Simulation uses: adding language-related delays to dispatch and response time models and to equity analyses of emergency medical services. Related records: the FCC 911 Master PSAP Registry (data-fcc-911-master-psap-registry) lists answering points.
